obligations.expected_behavior: For each destructive operation, explicitly declare the scope of resources or effects it can affect.
forbidden_result: The destructive operation is executed without an affected-scope declaration.
obligations.observable_result: The operation definition or request contains an explicit affected-scope declaration before execution.
obligations.state_after: The destructive operation has a recorded affected scope.
obligations.state_before: A destructive operation is being defined or requested.
obligations.subject: Destructive operation affected scope
obligations.trigger: A destructive operation is defined or requested.

obligations.expected_behavior: For each destructive operation, explicitly declare the required confirmation or authorization source.
forbidden_result: The operation omits the required confirmation or authorization source.
obligations.observable_result: The operation definition or request identifies the confirmation or authorization source required for execution.
obligations.state_after: The required confirmation or authorization source is recorded.
obligations.state_before: A destructive operation is being defined or requested.
obligations.subject: Destructive operation confirmation or authorization source
obligations.trigger: A destructive operation is defined or requested.

obligations.expected_behavior: For each destructive operation, disclose either the available recovery information or that the operation is irreversible.
forbidden_result: The operation provides neither recovery information nor an irreversibility disclosure.
obligations.observable_result: The operation documentation or request contains a recovery disclosure or an explicit irreversibility disclosure.
obligations.state_after: Recovery or irreversibility information is disclosed.
obligations.state_before: A destructive operation is being defined or requested.
obligations.subject: Destructive operation recovery or irreversibility disclosure
obligations.trigger: A destructive operation is defined or requested.

obligations.expected_behavior: Fail the destructive operation when its affected scope is missing.
forbidden_result: A destructive operation with missing scope succeeds.
A destructive effect is initiated despite the missing scope.
obligations.observable_result: The operation reports failure when no affected scope is declared.
obligations.state_after: The operation is failed because its affected scope is missing.
obligations.state_before: A destructive operation request lacks an affected-scope declaration.
obligations.subject: Missing-scope denial
obligations.trigger: A destructive operation is requested without an affected-scope declaration.

obligations.expected_behavior: Fail the destructive operation when a bypass flag is supplied as the basis for proceeding.
forbidden_result: A bypass flag causes the operation to proceed successfully.
The bypass flag circumvents the required confirmation or authorization control.
obligations.observable_result: The operation reports failure when a bypass flag is presented.
obligations.state_after: The operation is failed because a bypass flag was supplied.
obligations.state_before: A destructive operation request includes a bypass flag.
obligations.subject: Bypass-flag denial
obligations.trigger: A destructive operation is requested with a bypass flag.

obligations.expected_behavior: Fail the destructive operation when its confirmation is derived solely from untrusted input.
forbidden_result: Solely untrusted input is accepted as sufficient confirmation.
The operation proceeds successfully on the basis of solely untrusted confirmation.
obligations.observable_result: The operation reports failure when confirmation has no trusted session, user, or policy-authorized source.
obligations.state_after: The operation is failed because its confirmation source is solely untrusted input.
obligations.state_before: A destructive operation request has confirmation derived only from untrusted input.
obligations.subject: Untrusted-confirmation denial
obligations.trigger: A destructive operation presents confirmation derived solely from untrusted input.

obligations.expected_behavior: Accept existing session or user authorization as satisfying the authorization requirement when the owning policy accepts that authorization source.
forbidden_result: A policy-accepted existing session or user authorization is rejected solely because it is not a newly supplied confirmation.
The operation requires a different authorization source despite the owning policy accepting the existing authorization.
obligations.observable_result: The operation proceeds through authorization using the existing session or user authorization when the owning policy marks it valid.
obligations.state_after: The existing policy-accepted session or user authorization is accepted for the operation.
obligations.state_before: A destructive operation has an existing session or user authorization and the owning policy defines it as valid.
obligations.subject: Policy-accepted existing authorization
obligations.trigger: A destructive operation is authorized by an existing session or user authorization that the owning policy accepts.

obligations.expected_behavior: Do not require an additional confirmation solely as a universal extra step for every destructive operation when the owning policy already accepts the existing authorization.
forbidden_result: Every destructive operation is forced through a redundant confirmation regardless of the owning policy.
An additional confirmation is required when the existing authorization already satisfies the owning policy.
obligations.observable_result: No redundant confirmation step is imposed when the accepted existing authorization already fulfills the owning policy.
obligations.state_after: The operation uses the accepted authorization without an unnecessary extra confirmation.
obligations.state_before: The owning policy accepts an existing session or user authorization for the destructive operation.
obligations.subject: No redundant confirmation
obligations.trigger: An existing session or user authorization satisfies the owning policy for a destructive operation.
